questions.topic: Query Likelihood: Documents as Language Models
questions.question: What question does the query-likelihood model use for ranking?
options: How likely is the document's language model to generate the query?
How many other documents in the collection contain the query?
How likely is the whole collection model to generate this document?
How likely is the query's own language model to generate the document?

questions.topic: Query Likelihood: Documents as Language Models
questions.question: What is the maximum-likelihood estimate of a term probability in a document?
options: The term's collection frequency divided by the vocabulary size
The term's frequency in the document divided by its token count
The number of documents holding the term divided by the query length
The term's count in the query divided by the collection token count

questions.topic: Query Likelihood: Documents as Language Models
questions.question: Why are query-likelihood scores normally calculated in log space?
options: Logs restore the word order that the unigram assumption had discarded
Logs make every query term contribute the same amount to the final score
Logs remove the need to smooth terms that are missing from a document
Logs turn a product of small probabilities into a sum, avoiding underflow

questions.topic: Query Likelihood: Documents as Language Models
questions.question: Document A has 5 occurrences in 100 tokens and B has 5 in 1000. Which has the larger unsmoothed term probability?
options: A, with 0.05
B, with 0.005

They tie at 0.005

questions.topic: Query Likelihood: Documents as Language Models
questions.question: Why is query likelihood not itself the probability that a document is relevant?
options: It returns a value below zero once the scores are taken in log space
It measures compatibility with an estimated distribution, not usefulness
It is a probability over documents rather than over the query's terms
It becomes a relevance probability only after Bayes' rule is applied to it

questions.topic: Why Smoothing Is Mandatory: The Zero-Frequency Problem
questions.question: What happens to an unsmoothed product likelihood if one query term is absent from a document?
options: It falls back to the term's probability under the collection model
It drops by the term's inverse document frequency in the collection
It collapses to zero, whatever the remaining terms happen to have scored
It stays unchanged, because absent terms are dropped from the product

questions.topic: Why Smoothing Is Mandatory: The Zero-Frequency Problem
questions.question: What distribution usually supplies background probability during smoothing?
options: The distribution of ranks over the first page of retrieved results
The distribution of lengths across the documents in the collection
The distribution of terms inside the single highest-scoring document
The distribution of terms across the whole collection of documents

questions.topic: Why Smoothing Is Mandatory: The Zero-Frequency Problem
questions.question: If a term appears 10,000 times in a 100,000,000-token collection, what is its collection probability?

questions.topic: Why Smoothing Is Mandatory: The Zero-Frequency Problem
questions.question: Why does smoothing also help a term seen once in a very short document?
options: It removes the observation so the document model matches the collection
It pulls an unreliable extreme estimate toward the collection evidence
It normalizes the document length so short and long documents score alike
It raises the term's probability to one so the query can never score zero

questions.topic: Why Smoothing Is Mandatory: The Zero-Frequency Problem
questions.question: Why is adding the same arbitrary epsilon only to missing query terms a weak solution?
options: It always overflows in floating-point arithmetic once the query grows long
It inflates every document's token count, which distorts the length ratio
It leaves the model unnormalized and treats rare and common terms alike
It reproduces Dirichlet smoothing exactly, so it inherits the same failures

questions.topic: Why Smoothing Is Mandatory: The Zero-Frequency Problem
questions.question: A query term is absent from the entire collection. What extra policy is needed?
options: Fall back on the term's ordinary collection probability from the index
Assign every document the same score so the ranking stays unchanged
Drop the missing term silently, which is safe for a new product code
Cover it with unknown-token mass, subwords, correction, or rewriting

questions.question: What does lambda control in Jelinek-Mercer smoothing?
options: The fixed share of probability mass taken from the background collection model
The number of pseudo-tokens the collection prior contributes per document
The point at which the document model stops being used altogether
The count of expansion terms carried into the second retrieval pass

questions.question: What does mu represent in Dirichlet smoothing?
options: A mixture fraction that is constrained to lie between zero and one
A prior strength measured in pseudo-tokens added to a document
A count of the judged queries used to fit the smoothing rule
A fixed floor applied to every document's final ranking score

How does Dirichlet background influence change with document length at fixed mu?
options: It rises steadily as a document gets longer and its own counts grow
It sits at exactly one half for a document of any length at all
It stays flat, since the mixture weight ignores document length
It is stronger for shorter documents, whose evidence is sparser

questions.question: With length 100, tf 2, collection probability 0.001, and mu 1000, what is the Dirichlet probability?
options: Approximately 0.00273
Approximately 0.00182
Approximately 0.02000

questions.question: Why are lambda 0.2 and mu 0.2 not equivalent smoothing settings?
options: Jelinek-Mercer uses no collection model, so lambda cannot be compared
Lambda is a mixture fraction, while mu is a pseudo-count on the token scale
Mu is restricted to negative values, so 0.2 falls outside its range
Both parameters act on query length, so neither one touches the models
